claims.text: The heritage register attributes an operating Darwin–Java cable to 1871, a later backup and replacement, and wartime disruption in 1942. Opening, redundancy, replacement and interruption are different service facts. None establishes uninterrupted availability, sovereign legitimacy or a physical Dili cable. This proposed alternative concerns the actual named cable; it does not prove that other connections never existed or erase the people affected by war. Original service logs remain uncollated.

claims.text: Does a cable’s opening prove uninterrupted communication service or sovereignty over its endpoints? An actual named cable can open, gain backup, be replaced and be disrupted. Those records neither prove uninterrupted all-route communication nor establish Dili infrastructure or political sovereignty.
